title: Sell Mineral Rights in Loving County, TX/NM
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Loving County, TX
metaDescription: Loving County has under a hundred residents but sits on some of the densest horizontal drilling in the Delaware Basin. We buy minerals here directly, no listing required.
heroLead: Loving County is the least populated county in the United States and one of the most heavily drilled square miles in the entire Permian Basin, which makes it a strange place to own minerals.
intro: I've worked acreage all over the Delaware Basin and Loving County still stands out. There are more producing wellbores here than there are people, and most owners with an interest in this county don't live anywhere near Mentone, the county seat. A lot of these tracts trace back to ranching families who never expected the ground under their cattle to sit over some of the most active Wolfcamp and Bone Spring horizontal development in Texas.

Because so few people actually live on the surface here, mineral records can be thin on local knowledge, courthouse staff turnover is high, and title work sometimes takes patience. That's exactly the kind of situation we're set up to handle without slowing you down more than necessary.

sections.heading: Core Delaware Basin geology, no shelf to hide behind
paragraphs: Unlike a county like Lea or Eddy where you're dealing with a shelf side and a basin side, Loving County sits almost entirely in the deep, core Delaware Basin. That means stacked Wolfcamp and Bone Spring benches, thick Delaware sand intervals, and operators running multi-well pads that can hold six, eight, or more laterals under a single surface location. Well density here is about as high as anywhere in the Permian.

For an owner, that generally means more wells touching your acreage over time, which can mean more royalty checks, but it also means more spacing unit paperwork, more pooling orders, and more division order amendments to track. We check every unit your interest could be tied to rather than only the well you're currently getting paid on.

sections.heading: Why offers here move fast
paragraphs: With this much active permitting and drilling concentrated in one county, operators are often working several sections at once, and new permits can shift the value of a tract quickly. If we see a permit filed on an offset unit to your acreage, that changes our number, sometimes within weeks of the filing showing up.

That cuts both ways for a seller. If you're hoping a new well gets drilled near your tract before you sell, that can raise the price. If you'd rather lock in value now rather than wait through years of drilling and decline, that's a reasonable call too, and it's yours to make. We'll tell you honestly what nearby permitting suggests either way.

sections.heading: Out-of-state and multi-generation ownership
paragraphs: Given how few people actually live in Loving County, most of the mineral owners we talk to here are elsewhere, often several states away, holding an interest that came down through a ranching family or an old land trade. We handle closing entirely by mail and wire, you don't need to be anywhere near Mentone to sell.

If your interest was split among siblings or cousins decades ago and nobody's kept it organized since, we're used to piecing that together from the county clerk's real property records and Railroad Commission unit filings.

faqs.question: Loving County has almost no residents. How do you handle title work with so little local infrastructure?
faqs.answer: We pull directly from the county clerk's recorded instruments and Railroad Commission filings rather than relying on local knowledge. It can take a bit longer than a county with more staff, but it's routine for us.

faqs.question: Why is Loving County drilled so densely?
faqs.answer: It sits in the core of the Delaware Basin with thick, stacked Wolfcamp and Bone Spring pay, which supports multi-well pads with several laterals under one surface location. Well density here is among the highest in the Permian.

faqs.question: Should I wait to sell until a new well is permitted near my tract?
faqs.answer: It depends on your goals. New permitting nearby can raise value, but it's not guaranteed and can take years to produce a check. We'll give you an honest read on nearby activity so you can decide what fits your situation.

faqs.question: I don't live in Texas and have never been to Mentone. Can I still sell?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most of our Loving County sellers are in the same position. Closing happens by mail and wire transfer, no travel required.

faqs.question: How is a working interest in Loving County different to sell than a royalty interest?
faqs.answer: A working interest owner shares in drilling and operating costs, so we price it against net proceeds after those costs rather than gross royalty. Let us know which type of interest you hold and we'll quote it correctly the first time.

faqs.question: How do pooling orders affect a Loving County sale?
faqs.answer: With this much multi-well pad development, your acreage is often pooled into more than one spacing unit across different Wolfcamp and Bone Spring benches. We review every pooling order tied to your tract so the offer reflects everything you're actually entitled to, instead of only the most recent order you may have on file.

faqs.question: Can you close before the end of the year for tax planning purposes?
faqs.answer: We can move quickly once title is confirmed, but exact timing depends on your specific documentation. Let us know your target date early and we'll tell you honestly whether it's realistic for your interest.
